recipes.description: Distinct singleton palatal fricative; postmutation merger in a disclosed late holding zone.
recipes.assumptions: Singleton g is a fricative; gg/ng are stop classes. Broad incumbent eligibility is retained under Fulk's broader account rather than silently restricted to one positional table. Stops retain explicitly telescoped reflex proxies: ʧ/ʤ are not early phonetic affricates. New fricative does not trigger mutation. Merger is after mutation; its late holding zone is computational, not a source-established exact date.
recipes.limitations: Native key suffix contains an independently overbroad inherited-j vocalization proxy; the authoritative key/day discriminator is therefore assessed at the mutation checkpoint, not misreported as a complete native key derivation. No origin tags, grammatical exceptions, admissions or production change.

recipes.description: Delayed fricative merger plus bounded inherited-j retention after non-high long front monophthongs.
recipes.assumptions: Singleton g is a fricative; gg/ng are stop classes. Broad incumbent eligibility is retained under Fulk's broader account rather than silently restricted to one positional table. Stops retain explicitly telescoped reflex proxies: ʧ/ʤ are not early phonetic affricates. New fricative does not trigger mutation. Merger is after mutation; its late holding zone is computational, not a source-established exact date. The inherited-j normalization proxy excludes non-high long front monophthongs (Hogg1979 p.105: key); this is a source-led bounded restriction, not a claim that all remaining Vj environments undergo one physical vocalization.
recipes.limitations: No origin tags or grammatical conditioning. Late weak-suffix e-j normalization remains a disclosed telescoped proxy (RingeTaylor2014 p.228); this case does not adjudicate every inherited-j history or exact affrication date.
